what_this_is: the destination plane's cost against the alternatives, measured before the format is argued rather than after

uint8_palette.why_not: 432 distinct destinations are named and a uint8 palette holds at most 254. A plane whose width depends on the data is also a format that breaks silently when the data changes, so this is not merely unavailable today -- it is the wrong shape for a published format

uint16_plane_renumbered_by_first_appeara.why_this_one_is_free: it changes which integer names a destination and nothing else. The side table is written in the same order either way, so there is no decode cost and no contract change -- if it wins, there is no trade to weigh

the_decision_and_why: SHIP THE uint16 PLANE, and not because it is cheapest -- it is not. Column-major run-length is 28,027 against the plane's 38,505, so the plane costs 10,478 bytes more, 4.1% of the bundle. The reason is the ACCESS PATTERN: a card reads ONE cell's destination, the cell a household is pointing at, where the value and status planes are read for every cell on every repaint. Expanding 330,502 run-length entries to answer a single lookup is backwards, and a prefix index to avoid that is a second structure to ship and validate. A plane answers in O(1) with no decode step at all
the_free_option_measured_and_declined: renumbering the ordinals by first appearance saves 314 bytes, 0.8% of the plane. That is noise. It is declined not because it costs anything but because adopting it would add an ordinal-assignment step between the raster and the table for no real gain, and every such step is a place the two can drift apart
what_this_does_not_settle: phone latency, which is unmeasured and on the release prerequisite list. The argument above is about where work belongs rather than how much there is
